name: 9 V power · battery, switched by the input jack
description: How a battery-only pedal takes its 9 V and switches it off: the battery's + is V+, its − goes to the stereo input jack's ring (J1), so the battery is on only while a mono guitar cable is in, which is why battery pedals say to unplug them when not in use. Wire J1's T (the in port) to IN's middle; then pulling the cable in Knobs (Input cable) turns the pedal off, and the render is refused until it's back in. Then the 9 V input filter to V+F (its values from the ProCo Rat, ElectroSmash). The battery's form sets how drained it is. The same V+F as the other power blocks.

parts.note: A stereo input jack switching the battery: its − goes to the ring, and a mono guitar plug's long sleeve joins the ring to ground, so the pedal is on only with a cable in. A stereo cable doesn't switch it on (its ring is its own). Wire T (the in port) to IN's middle, so pulling the cable takes the guitar out too. Knobs: Input cable.
parts.label: Input
